key_insight: Preserving recovered execution procedures in reusable artifacts raises ML reproduction success while reducing downstream API spending.
engineering_relevance: Packaging code, environment setup, experiment launchers, and a reproduction guide can make research handoffs more reliable across coding agents.
method: ReproBridge constructs standardized, refined artifacts from research code and recovered procedures.
Agents attempt reproduction in fresh sessions using raw code or refined artifacts.
A separate Auditor checks execution evidence.
evidence_signal: Across four models on ReproBridge-Bench's 1,029 tasks from 387 experiments across 36 papers, refined artifacts increased mean success from 76.4% to 92.6% and reduced downstream API spending by 19.7% on average.
watch_item: Reported downstream API savings do not establish whether they offset the upfront cost of constructing and validating refined artifacts.
paper_title: ReproBridge: Building Reproducibility into ML Research Artifacts
